directive_handled.title: Integrity wall-clock + cost audit
directive_handled.headline: Integrity cost ($4.24/run, $21/wk) is real and stable and worth engineering. BUT the directive's '65 min/run' wall-clock premise is a skewed-mean artifact: 5 of 6 runs are 7.5-10 min (median 9.7 min); the mean is dragged to 56 min by ONE 2026-06-19 run at 17462s (4.85h), almost certainly a Check-3/Check-5b network stall. Cost is decoupled from wall-clock (the 4.85h run cost only ~12% above median).
directive_handled.cost_composition: cache_read 55.1% / cache_write_1h 29.2% / output 15.7% (matches directive's table). Driver = ~70-turn prefix re-read on a large cold-cached 855-line prompt (PROP-104 the_correction pattern).
directive_handled.recommendation: Sequence 1C (Check-3 weekly + timeout budget — fixes the stall, immediate) -> 1A (precompute-extract mechanical checks into compute-integrity-mechanical.js, est 25-40% cut, model-independent, LOW risk) -> 1B (prompt-slim rare-path prose) -> re-measure -> only then consider 1D (Haiku split). Lead with precompute+gating, NOT the Haiku split.
corrections_filed: Wall-clock 65-min is a one-outlier skewed mean; median ~9.7 min.
Haiku is ~3x cheaper than Sonnet (cache_read $0.10 vs $0.30), NOT 10x as the directive's Q3 framing implied.
docs/index.html is 1.75MB, not the 4.5MB the directive cited.
